ruling.recommended_action: Refer the case file to Trust & Safety for human review of the driver's message [F12]; do not rule on the $5.00 no-show fee; consider interim suspension of the driver's account pending review (SAFE-4) and notify the rider via RydeHELP.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: Chat #3 at 17:15 from the driver reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F12]. Read as a careful person would, that is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider — not a pickup arrangement and not a mere "hurry up". It is the last message before the driver cancelled at 17:15:30 [F4]. Under SAFE-1 (§5.2) any dispute whose chat contains a threat must be flagged for immediate human escalation regardless of the dispute type filed, and SAFE-3 bars me from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome on it. I therefore do not decide the no-show fee.

For the reviewer's file, the underlying no-show elements appear provable on the record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:10:00 at 40 m from pickup and stayed within 200 m for 5 min 30 s ([F6], [F7], [F1], [F2]); the 5-minute free wait from arrival had passed by the 17:15:30 cancellation [F4]; he sent 2 in-app messages (first 17:10:30) and made 1 in-app call (first 17:11:30) before cancelling ([F5], [F10], [F14]); continuous presence is shown by GPS [F3]. The rider's "2 min, coming" at 17:12 [F11] does not extend the free wait. The app reason was rider_no_show [F4] and his statement [F15] is consistent, so NS-1 vs NS-3 on its face points to NS-1.

However, the threat changes the path: SAFE-1/SAFE-2 send the matter to human review, and NS-1 is conditional on the record's integrity being assessed by a human in a case involving driver misconduct — I do not clear the $5.00 fee here. Note that the driver's written statement [F15] omits the aggressive message entirely, which the reviewer should weigh.

Evidence status: sufficient for the safety screen (all chat is timestamped [F13]) and for the NS-1 mechanics; no traffic data available ([F16], [F17]) but no route issue is in play, so nothing outcome-relevant is missing. Confidence in the escalation is high; the fee outcome is left to the human reviewer.
